'''Turning Traitor''' (Japanese: {{hl|不忠の徒|Fuchū no to}} ''The Disloyal One'') is the tenth chapter of [[Ephraim]]'s route in {{FE8}}.

==Plot==
{{main|Turning Traitor/Script}}

As [[Ephraim]] marches to the capital of [[Grado]], a messenger comes bearing news of [[Eirika]]; an uprising in [[Carcino]] put [[Innes]] in danger, and Eirika traveled to assist him. Ephraim reasons that the best way to help Eirika is to end the war by defeating Grado. Then, a minor earthquake occurs; [[Seth]] informs Ephraim that such quakes are common in Grado, and Ephraim remembers a similar quake when he first visited Grado.

At Bethroen, [[Selena (The Sacred Stones)|Selena]] catches up to [[Duessel]]; when he expresses reluctance to fight Ephraim, she informs him that he has been accused of treason and prepares to execute him. Duessel resists, and Selena instructs [[Cormag]] to drive them into the sea, though Cormag is reluctant to Fight Duessel.

As the battle starts, [[Valter]] arrives and relieves Selena of duty; he tells her Emperor [[Vigarde]] no longer finds her trustworthy enough to deal with Duessel. Selena departs for the capital to verify his claims, and Valter instates [[Beran]] to defeat Duessel and Ephraim. Cormag considers whether or not to attack Duessel, but eventually convinces himself to move out and fight.

During the Battle, Ephraim can talk to Duessel. Ephraim asks Duessel to go with him, but Duessel is reluctant, having served Grado his whole life, now branded a traitor; Ephraim convinces Duessel that living as a traitor will do Grado more good than accepting death, and Duessel agrees to go with him. Additionally, Duessel or Tana can speak with Cormag. Duessel accepts Cormag's judgement as a knight sent to kill him, but Cormag cannot believe Duessel is a traitor at heart and joins him. Alternately, Tana gets Cormag to stop fighting, and attempts to understand why he is fighting Duessel; Cormag is frustrated by her refusal to leave him, but is convinced to speak with Duessel by her continued insistence.

If Beran is not defeated, after some time passes, he decides to flee, fearing Valter's anger at his failure to defeat Duessel or Ephraim. Duessel and Ephraim then reconvene, and Ephraim asks why Vigarde started the war. Duessel states that Vigarde changed significantly when [[Lyon]] created something he called the "[[Dark Stone (object)|Dark Stone]]", which he claimed to be more powerful than the [[Sacred Stone (object)|Sacred Stone]]s. [[Myrrh]] states that the dark power she felt may be able to corrupt people, and Duessel states that Lyon has the Dark Stone in the capital. Duessel insists on accompanying Ephraim to the capital, in spite of fighting his countryman. If Duessel's ally NPCs survived, they ask to accompany the [[Frelia]]n Army to aid Duessel.

Seth informs Ephraim that a ship is being readied for them, and Ephraim orders his men to rest while they wait. Then, [[L'Arachel]] approaches Ephraim; L'Arachel informs him that a "phantom ship" is roaming the waters, scaring off sailors. L'Arachel then leaves with her retainers to find and defeat the phantom ship. Once she leaves, Ephraim's ship arrives, and his army prepares to set sail.

==Strategy==
{{strategy}}
The first priority is to reach the green units as soon as possible. The two soldiers and possibly mercenary near the start can be eliminated easily and quickly by putting a unit on the forest tile to their right and sticking everyone else just outside of range. After that the two tile gap where the soldiers initially stood can be occupied by two sword users to deal with the fighters. Depending on your team composition this may require setting up a rescue before hand, but most teams should have units capable and in a pinch one can do but it requires leaving the rest of the team further back. After that move quickly into the center, send a group to eliminate the pirates, and another to start tearing up the enemies near the boss, while keeping in mind that a large wave of mounted reinforcements will show up from where you started on turn 6. While several enemies near the boss are equipped with scary weapons, they will not move even if a unit is put in their range making them safe to remove at your leisure. Once the pirates are dealt with nothing else will attack from the south, freeing up any units assigned to them other tasks. While the forts that spawn mercenaries can be blocked to prevent their spawning, they have low offensive power and can't get past the bridge in a single turn. This allows for certain speedy lance users that can take a hit (on average [[Ephraim]], [[Franz]], and possibly [[Seth]] can do this at a reasonable level, depending on speed rolls, even on Difficult) to wait on the isolated forest then kill on the counter attack for a nice source of experience.

The fleets are weak enough they are generally only a hazard to non-combat units and fliers. Cormag can one round the Secret Book fleet at base if he can get in range, though this will generally require baiting it to expend its ammo first, at least three of its five shots will generally be expended on your approach so leaving a unit to provoke the other two isn't unreasonable. When injured, the AI for the allied cavaliers will frequently retreat to the left village and not move. Getting the [[Hero Crest]] under this condition will necessitate a flyer to rescue them.

Obtaining the [[Knight Crest]] at the end of the chapter requires that ''all'' of [[Duessel]]'s units survive. As such, deploying mounted units to handle the pirates southward is highly recommended. Being a [[Objectives#Survive.2Fdefend|survival]] chapter, it is not required to kill [[Beran]], and one may want to obtain the [[Horseslayer]] ([[Armorslayer]] in the Japanese version), [[Killing Edge]], and even the [[Secret Book]] before doing so if they wish. [[Cormag]] will stay away from the battle until turn 4, so speaking with Duessel or even deploying [[Tana]] is key to recruiting him. 

While it is improbable for Duessel to fall unless poor decisions are made, his defeat will result in a [[Game Over]].

==Trivia==
*This is the only chapter in {{FE8}}, as well as the {{FES}}, to feature [[Fleet]]s.
*[[Marisa]] makes a cameo appearance when visiting the southern [[village]].
*Even if a player manages to kill Selena (impossible as neither [[siege tome]]s nor [[Warp (staff)|Warp]] nor [[Swiftsole]]s are available at this point) before Valter sends her away after their first turn, she will still appear in [[Fluorspar's Oath|Chapter&nbsp;13]].
